### Socket protects your app from malicious dependencies lurking in your open source supply chain.

Open source code makes up 90% of most codebases. It is critical to manage it effectively to reduce your security risk.

## Detect and block open source supply chain attacks

Security teams depend on Socket to prevent malicious open source dependencies from infiltrating their apps.

Socket dramatically improves your open source security posture by _detecting and blocking the attacks you don't expect_ – malware, install scripts, hidden code, typo-squatting, and more – which aren't caught by traditional vulnerability scanners.

- **Block malware** – Block emerging malware threats

- **Block typo-squatting** – Block malicious packages that differ in name by only a few characters, and recommend the correct package

- **Detect hidden code** – Detect obfuscated, minified, or hidden code

- **Detect privileged API usage** – Report when a dependency update introduces new risky API usage – filesystem, network, child_process, eval()

- **Detect suspicious updates** – Sudden inclusion of privileged APIs in patch or minor releases

Socket currently [supports 80+ detections](https://socket.dev/alerts) in 5 categories: supply chain risk, quality, maintenance, known vulnerabilities, and license problems.

## Take charge of your dependency health

Socket improves security outcomes and reduces work for security teams by **surfacing actionable security information directly inline in GitHub** so developers are empowered to make better decisions.

- **Five minute deployment** – The easiest security product you'll ever deploy in your organization. Just install a GitHub app and you're done.

- **Provide security feedback directly on PRs** – Empower developers to solve security issues before they're deployed into production.

- **Automated security** – Spend security team resources auditing the highest-impact dependencies, instead of all or nothing.

## Socket detects what vulnerability scanners can’t

It's no longer sufficient to scan for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and stop there. And yet, that's what the leading "supply chain security" products do, leaving you vulnerable.

It can take weeks or months for a CVE to be discovered, reported, and detected by tools. But in today's culture of fast development, a malicious dependency can be updated, merged, and running in production in days or even sometimes hours.

Defenders need a new approach to address emerging threats from malicious dependencies:

- **Maintainer intentionally added malware** – Rogue maintainer sabotaged his own open source package with 100M downloads/month, affecting companies such as Amazon AWS

- **Package hijacked and poisoned w/ cryptominers and password-stealing malware** – Deliberate malware introduced into multiple packages with 30M downloads/month each

- **Package hijacked to add backdoor targeting a specific organization** – Obfuscated malware added to a dependency which targeted a single company, went undetected for over a week, and made it into their production build

- **NPM package manager allowed anyone to publish new versions of any package** – Attackers could publish new versions of any NPM package without authorization _for multiple years_

Using third-party dependencies without proper vetting leaves you open to hacking, breaches, and assorted security misfortune.

## Deep review — PR #208 (`consolidation: accepted PRs & branches for 0.1.6`)

Reviewed head `51621823bb4ba29d0b23019b38845476c7cbf56f` against base `0.1.6` (`3a37f92`) — **1 commit, 1,039 files, +210,495 / −19,219**. Process: `REVIEW.md` → `FULL-REVIEW.md` fetched from `main` (Part I procedure, Part II risk catalog; Parts III–IV non-normative), then six independent passes — (A) persistence/migrations, (B) security/authority, (C) frontend + IPC contracts, (D) CI/CD + release, (E) test validity, (F) cross-cutting verification — with each candidate finding re-checked against the Phase 7 five-condition gate. Every finding below was re-derived independently in the final pass; the two I could test empirically were tested, and one earlier hypothesis (a dropped `pull_request` trigger) was **withdrawn** because the base was already push-only.

---

## Verdict

**Status:** Not Ready
**Confidence:** Medium-High — code analysis and the high-risk traces are complete and two gates were independently re-run; Rust/cargo and the full vitest suites were not executed locally (no toolchain in this environment) and are taken from CI on this exact SHA.
**Mergeable:** No (blocked by F1)
**CI verification:** Passing — every check green on `5162182` (`Build Desktop` ×3 OS, `Lint Desktop` ×3, `Desktop Rust/TS Unit`, `Desktop Integration`, `i18n Catalog Sync`, `i18n Extractor Idempotence`, `Rust Transcription` ×3, `Repo-wide Prettier`, `Gitleaks updater-key scan`, `SonarCloud`, `CodeAnt SAST/SCA/Quality Gates`). Review decision on the PR is bot `APPROVED`.

**Blunt summary:** the engineering inside this PR is largely excellent — the migration consolidation, the audio-import TOCTOU fix, the manual-installer verification chain and the SSRF plumbing are the best work in the diff. But a 1,039-file consolidation is exactly where a *one-line-class* miss hides, and there is one: a capability rewrite that dropped every plaintext origin while a production call site still uses the plugin that consumes that capability. That breaks the documented local Ollama path. Four small fixes unblock this; there is no need to re-split the PR.

---

## 1. Change inventory

| Area | Changed contract | Risk | Required verification | Result |
| ---- | ---------------- | ---- | --------------------- | ------ |
| `db/migrations/069_*` + `db/consolidation.rs` + `db/open.rs` | 0.1.5 → 0.1.6 schema upgrade; ledger retirement 71–88; 5 tables rebuilt | **Critical** | Fresh + upgrade + intermediate-build replay, rollback, cascade check | **Verified** (F3 aside) |
| `capabilities/default.json`, `csp` in `tauri.conf.json` | Which origins may fetch, and whether via plugin-http or Rust | **Critical** | Scope/consumer trace for every fetch call site | **Failed → F1** |
| `commands.rs` `download_and_open_mac_installer` | New command that downloads **and opens** a release artifact | **Critical** | URL allow-list, redirect policy, size caps, signature-before-open | **Verified sound** (F4 nit) |
| `commands.rs` `private_http_request` / `openai_compatible_http_request` | Rust-mediated egress with IP pinning, `no_proxy`, redirect validation | **Critical** | Rejected-input + redirect tests | **Verified sound** |
| `tauri.conf.json` updater block | Updater trust anchor + endpoint | **Critical** | Config contract test, release workflow injection | **Verified sound** (F2 residual) |
| `build-desktop.yml` | Removes a committed updater **private** key literal | **Critical** | Secret scan; history exposure | **Fixed by this PR** (rotate — §4) |
| `generate-text.repo.ts` | Post-processing/chat egress for Ollama + OpenAI-compatible | **High** | Consumer trace to capability scope | **Failed → F1** |
| `db/open.rs` downgrade guard | Unconfigured ledger versions | High | Newer-version DB must not be quarantined | **Verified sound** (F3 residual) |
| `redaction.utils.ts` | Recursive masking, cycles, secret patterns | High | Nested/array/cyclic + `__proto__` handling | **Verified sound** |
| `rust_pill_shared/src/drag.rs` (new, 1,252 lines) + 3 platform pills | Drag/settle geometry, clamping | High | Cross-platform tests, off-screen probes | **Verified sound** (has the specific centre/half-off-screen test) |
| `release.yml` | Signed updater manifest, beta + stable channels, signature verification gate | High | Release-shell contract tests, key injection | **Verified sound** |
| `featureFlags.ts` / `preferences_queries.rs` | Atomic SQLite CAS for expansion flags | High | Concurrency/retry tests | **Verified sound** |
| i18n locales (10 files) | 958 message keys | Medium | Key parity across locales | **Verified independently** |
| `apps/preview/**` (76 files, new workspace app) | New dev-only surface | Medium | Isolated? path filters? | **Verified isolated** → F8 |
| `reports/pr207/**` (67 files) + root agent artifacts | Committed review evidence/scratch | Low | Secret hygiene | **No secrets found** → F7 |
| `docs/**` (16 deletions, 5 competitor-research additions) | Documentation surface | Low | Stated-exclusion consistency | **Failed → F6** |
| `.microreview.yml` | Deleted | Low | Target-branch commit containment | **Failed → F5** |

---

## 2. Findings

### 🟠 F1 — [High] The `http:default` narrowing kills Ollama / OpenAI-compatible post-processing

**Location:** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json` (removed old lines 64–71), `apps/desktop/src/repos/generate-text.repo.ts:189,210,231`

**Diff cause.** #208 rewrote the `http:default` capability and deleted *every* plaintext entry: `http://localhost`, `http://localhost/**`, `http://localhost:*`, `http://localhost:*/**` and the four `http://127.0.0.1*` equivalents. The new inline comment asserts that loopback/RFC1918/`*.local` endpoints "are routed through the `private_http_request` command".

**Evidence.**
- Upstream `tauri-plugin-http/permissions/default.toml`: `http:default` "enables all fetch operations but does **not** allow explicitly any origins to be fetched. This needs to be manually configured before usage." So the capability `allow` list *is* the complete scope.
- Upstream `scope.rs::is_allowed` is `allowed.iter().any(|e| e.url.test(url))` with no fallback; a non-matching URL yields `Error::UrlNotAllowed` → `"url not allowed on the configured scope: {url}"` (`plugins/http/src/error.rs`).
- `tauri.conf.json` has no `plugins.http` block, so nothing re-adds a scope.
- The migration to `secureFetch` was **incomplete**. Every other call site is covered (`transcribe-audio.repo.ts`, `model-provider.repo.ts`, `ollama.repo.ts`, `openrouter.repo.ts`, `GroqModelPicker.tsx`, `utils/speaches.utils.ts`, `utils/ollama.utils.ts` all import `secureFetch as fetch`), but `generate-text.repo.ts:37` imports plugin-http's `fetch as tauriFetch` and the shared `OpenAICompatibleBaseGenerateTextRepo` passes it as `customFetch` at lines 210 and 231.
- `customFetch` is honoured: `createClient(apiKey, baseUrl, customFetch)` (`voice-ai/src/openai.utils.ts:86,249`).

**Reachable scenario.** Default config, no user action beyond choosing Ollama for post-processing: `OLLAMA_DEFAULT_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:11434"` (`utils/ollama.utils.ts:3`) → `repos/index.ts:215,225` → `OllamaGenerateTextRepo("http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1")` → plugin-http → **denied**. `apps/docs/src/content/docs/providers/ollama.md:10` documents that base URL as the default; `docker-ollama.md:103` points users at the same URL. Any OpenAI-compatible key saved with an `http://` base URL fails identically, including chat streaming.

**Impact.** Core-flow failure for the documented local-only / self-hosted setup: post-processing and chat over Ollama (and plaintext OpenAI-compatible endpoints) error out at the scope check. Users see the raw plugin error and no obvious cause, and the failure is invisible to CI because the capability contract test *codifies* the removal and only scans `https://api.*` literals.

**Required change.** In `OpenAICompatibleBaseGenerateTextRepo`, pass `secureFetch` (not `tauriFetch`) as `customFetch` for both `generateText` and `streamChat`, matching `transcribe-audio.repo.ts`. Do **not** re-add the loopback scope entries — the http branch of `secureFetch` routes to `private_http_request`, which is the enforcement point this PR deliberately built.

**Verification.** (a) Unit test that the ollama and openai-compatible repos hand `secureFetch` to `openaiGenerateTextResponse`/`openaiStreamChat` (fails today, passes after the fix). (b) Extend `csp-capability.contract.test.ts` so the host scan covers **all** URL literals reaching a plugin-http call site, not just `https://api.*`, and assert each is in the capability scope. (c) Manual: Ollama post-processing + an `http://` OpenAI-compatible key.

### 🟡 F2 — [Medium] Unsigned builds advertise an update they can never install

**Location:** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:74,76`

The endpoint is now live while `pubkey` stays `""` (asserted on purpose by `tauri-conf.test.ts`, together with `createUpdaterArtifacts: false`). This fails **closed**, so it is not an RCE: upstream `Update::download` ends in `verify_signature(...)` → `base64_to_string("")` → `PublicKey::decode("")` → `Err`, so nothing can be installed. But `Updater::check()` performs no verification, so every build that does not receive `secrets.UPDATER_*` — `build-desktop.yml` CI artifacts (which this PR also gives `--features debug-assist`), forks, local `pnpm tauri build` — fetches `latest.json`, shows *"Version X is ready to install"*, then fails with a cryptic minisign error; the macOS manual fallback refuses with `"Updater public key is not configured"`.

**Required change.** Patch endpoint and pubkey together in `release.yml`, or keep `endpoints: []` until a key is injected; alternatively, have `checkForAppUpdates` present an explicit "no update channel in this build" state when the pubkey is empty. **Verification:** config invariant test — non-empty endpoints ⇒ non-empty pubkey.

### 🟡 F3 — [Medium] The 71..=88 exemption permanently disables the downgrade guard for the range 0.1.6 just vacated

**Location:** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/db/open.rs:188`

Unconfigured ledger rows in `71..=88` are deleted and skipped instead of raising *"the database was likely created by a newer version of the app"*. Correct for the intermediate superfix builds — but unconditional and permanent. The namespace now jumps `068 → 069`, so `071`–`088` are the obvious next numbers (and `db/mod.rs` already documents `021`/`070` as deliberately absent, i.e. this repo does leave and reuse gaps). If a later release uses version 71, a 0.1.6 client opening that newer database silently deletes its ledger row and treats its schema as absent — destroying the guard and risking a destructive re-apply on the way forward.

**Required change.** Make retirement identity-based: the ledger stores `description`, so retire only rows whose description matches the known folded set (`remove_cloud_modes`, `drop_is_enterprise`, `pill_reset_monitor_strategy`, `always_request_admin_on_startup`, …), and add a guard that `071`–`088` must never be reused. **Verification:** test that `(71, "some_future_migration")` is *not* retired while the known folded descriptions are.

### 🔵 F4 — [Low] `open` is spawned and never reaped; a failed hand-off is reported as success

**Location:** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs:4668`

`Command::new("open").arg(&dest).spawn()` drops the `Child` without `wait()`, leaving a zombie for the app's lifetime (the exact subprocess trap in the Part II catalog). `spawn()` only proves creation: if `open` then fails (no handler, mount refused, cancel), the command still returns `Ok(())`, the UI says `installing`, and the verified DMG stays in the temp dir — the cleanup branch runs only when `spawn` itself errors.

**Required change.** `wait()` on the child (inside `spawn_blocking`, like the verification already is) and remove `dest` on a non-zero status.

### 🔵 F5 — [Low] The consolidation silently reverts the target branch's tip commit

**Location:** `.microreview.yml` (deleted)

The file was added by `3a37f92 "chore: add MicroReview configuration"` — the *immediate parent* of the squashed commit and the current head of `0.1.6` — and #208 deletes it. That is the classic squashed-consolidation failure mode: the branch was built from a state predating the newest target-branch commit. `main` does not carry the file either, so it may well be intentional; if so, say so in the description. Either way, nothing in CI asserts that a consolidation head contains every commit of its target branch — add that check (`git rev-list`/containment) so the next consolidation cannot lose target-branch work silently.

### 🔵 F6 — [Low / process] The stated exclusions are not actually excluded

The body says *"Rejected and excluded: #144 (competitor docs)"*, and PR #144 (CLOSED) is *"docs: add competitor research (Vowen, Wispr Flow, TypeWhisper) + gap analysis"* touching `docs/competitor-research/**`. This PR nevertheless adds `docs/competitor-research/implementation-plans/` — 5 files, 558 lines (`expansion-program-status`, `shared-foundations`, `shared-foundations-decisions`, `shared-foundations-research`, `shared-foundations-verification`). Drop them or correct the description; a reviewer cannot reconcile "excluded" with the diff.

**Credit:** the *code* exclusions did hold — I confirmed no `meeting_queries.rs`, `meeting.repo.ts`, `meeting.actions.ts` or `automation_server.rs` from #151/#199 is present at head, and the retained `meetingNotesEnabled` flag is only a flag.

### 🔵 F7 — [Low / hygiene] ~2.5 MB of agent process artifacts on a release branch

`fully read this.txt.txt` (14,229 lines / 1.27 MB session transcript), `CORRECTIVE-REVIEW.md` (60 KB), `agent-prompt.md` (35 KB), `AUTO-LEARN-DICTIONARY-REVIEW.md` (34 KB), `PHASE3_CONSOLIDATION_REPORT.md`, `PREVIEW-SITE.md`, `docs/Installing-cargo-toolchain-for-kilocode-bot-agents-in-a-linux-sandbox.md`, and `reports/pr207/**` (67 files, ~80,800 lines, `accepted-feedback-index.json` = 743 KB).

**Positive:** I scanned the transcript for credential-shaped material (`sk-*`, `ghp_*`, `AKIA*`, PEM blocks, quoted passwords/API keys) — nothing found — and `.gitleaksignore` was correctly rewritten to fingerprints-only with path exclusions moved to `gitleaks.toml`. Still, these should not ship; they bloat every clone and tag and conflict with `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

A neat illustration of the cost: of the 10 inline comments I attempted on this review, 9 posted and the one anchored on `fully read this.txt.txt` was rejected by GitHub with `pull_request_review_thread.diff_entry: "fully read this.txt.txt diff is too large"`. The file is large enough that the platform will not render it as a diff — so it cannot be reviewed at all.

### 🔵 F8 — [Low / scope] A new 76-file workspace app rides along

`apps/preview` (`@maus-inc/preview`, `registry.ts` = 1,685 lines, `write-specs.mjs` = 1,011 lines) is properly isolated — nothing under `apps/desktop` imports it, so the shipped bundle is unaffected — but it expands the install/turbo/release surface and `CONTRIBUTING.md` explicitly lists scope-expanding PRs as least likely to be accepted. It is also only wired into `test-desktop-unit.yml` path filters; `lint-desktop.yml` and `build-desktop.yml` omit `apps/preview/**`. Split it out, or at least add `apps/preview/**` to the lint filter.

---

## 3. Correct behavior confirmed (verified, not assumed)

These are the parts I actively tried to break and could not:

1. **Migration consolidation + retirement — verified empirically.** I replayed the real migration set (`1..68` → `consolidation.rs`'s save/raw/restore → `069`) in `node:sqlite` for three profiles. Fresh install: all 69 steps apply. 0.1.5 upgrade with seeded rows: no column loss beyond the intended `is_enterprise` drop; `transcriptions` 21→25, `tones` 5→8, `user_profiles` 25→26, `api_keys` 14→15 (additions only); every index survives; payloads (ciphertext, audio path, cohort, streak, remote columns) intact; stored `cloud` modes rewritten to `local`/`none`. Intermediate build (`071`–`074` + all `075`–`088` columns): applies cleanly **and** the folded values round-trip — `preserve_audio_on_failure=0`, `expansion_flags`, `update_channel='beta'`, `pill_placement='top'`, `hands_free_delay_ms`, `review_before_insert`, `agent_enabled_tools`, tone `category`/`output_length`/`example_input_output`, `api_keys.transcription_path`, transcription `post_process_*`, `user_profiles.interaction_feedback_volume`. The `DROP TABLE` + `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` implicit-delete hazard is also clear: the only FK in the schema is `chat_messages.conversation_id → conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` and nothing references the five rebuilt tables. Running the whole file **plus** the retirements in one transaction, and classifying a newer-version database as `Other` rather than `Integrity` so it is *not* quarantined, are the two decisions that make this safe — that is the right call and it directly protects user data.
2. **Native audio-import TOCTOU.** `open_audio_import_file` resolves through a capability directory (`Dir::open_ambient_dir`), opens with `FollowSymlinks::No` + `nonblock(true)`, confirms `metadata.is_file()`, and rejects Windows reparse points — the returned handle is confined at open time, so later path changes cannot redirect it. This closes the race named in the description.
3. **Manual macOS installer chain.** https-only; `github.com` + `/maus-inc/mausVoice/releases/download/` pinning; per-hop redirect validation capped at 10; 250 MiB streaming cap enforced per chunk (not just `Content-Length`); a dedicated 16 KiB signature cap; temp file created with `create_new` and a random name; minisign verification against the embedded key **before** `open`; the file is deleted on every failure path; and it fails closed when the pubkey is empty.
4. **SSRF / proxy-bypass plumbing.** Every `fetch` in desktop + `voice-ai` routes through `secureFetch` (http → `private_http_request`, curated https → plugin-http). My first grep appeared to find un-migrated call sites; they were aliases (`secureFetch as fetch`) — the migration is complete except for F1.
5. **Beta channel hand-off.** `check_for_channel_update` registers the `Update` via `webview.resources_table().add(update)`; Tauri's `AppManager` holds a single app-wide `Arc<Mutex<ResourceTable>>`, so plugin-updater's `download_and_install` reads the same table — install/verify/relaunch run the stock path. Channel → manifest URL is a fixed match, so the `channel` argument cannot be used for SSRF.
6. **Updater trust remediation.** The committed `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` literal is removed from `build-desktop.yml`; `createUpdaterArtifacts: false` + empty pubkey + secret-injected key; `tauri-conf.test.ts` and the release-shell contract tests pin all of it. This is a real improvement — see §4 for the residual.
7. **i18n and contract scripts, independently reproduced.** 958 keys × 10 locales with **0** missing and **0** extra (my own parser, not theirs). `node --test scripts/ci/*.test.mjs` → **180/180 pass, 38 suites** — matching the PR body's claim exactly.
8. **No dangling edits.** `AgentActivity.tsx` and `MoreSettingsDialog.tsx` were deleted with no remaining imports; all new commands (`private_http_request`, `openai_compatible_http_request`, `check_for_channel_update`, `download_and_open_mac_installer`, `check_app_location_writable`, `set_menu_icon`, …) are registered in `app.rs` and present in the generated `bindings.ts`.
9. **Pill geometry.** The catalog's half-width/centre trap is explicitly covered (`rust_pill_shared/src/lib.rs` has `a_button_with_its_centre_inside_still_loses_its_hidden_half`), and clamping uses inclusive frame bounds with a settle snap.

---

## 4. Verification performed

| Check | Status | Evidence |
| ----- | ------ | -------- |
| Migration replay: fresh / 0.1.5 upgrade / intermediate build | **Passed (E3)** | Own `node:sqlite` harness replaying the real registry + `consolidation.rs` algorithm on head `5162182` |
| Column-loss + index + FK-cascade analysis of 069 | **Passed (E3)** | Same harness; only FK is `chat_messages → conversations` |
| i18n key parity (10 locales) | **Passed (E3)** | Own parser: 958 keys, 0 missing / 0 extra |
| `node --test scripts/ci/*.test.mjs` | **Passed (E3)** | 180 tests / 38 suites, 0 failures — matches PR claim |
| `apps/desktop/scripts/*.test.mjs` (7 files) | **Inconclusive locally** | `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: vitest` — extracted review tree has no `node_modules`; green in CI |
| `cargo clippy` / `cargo test` / pill crates | **Not run** | No Rust toolchain in this environment; CI green (Rust unit, transcription ×3 OS) |
| `pnpm check-types` / `lint` / `test:unit` / `test:integration` | **Not run locally** | CI green on this SHA; would require disturbing the checked-out working tree |
| `check-bindings.sh` / `gen:bindings` | **Not run** | CI `Test Desktop Unit` includes the bindings guard; new commands present in `bindings.ts` |
| Upstream semantics: plugin-updater `verify_signature`, plugin-http scope, Tauri resource table | **Passed (E4-source)** | Upstream v2 sources read directly to confirm fail-closed verification, scope semantics, and app-wide resource table |
| Desktop E2E (macOS manual installer, pill drag, Ollama flow) | **Not run** | No desktop runtime available |
| Workflow inspection (triggers, permissions, path filters, secret exposure) | **Passed (E2)** | All changed workflows reviewed; base was already push-only, so no trigger regression |

---

## 5. Assumptions and unknowns

- The Rust, clippy, full-vitest and packaging gates are **taken from CI on this exact SHA**, not re-executed here. `REVIEW.md`/`AGENTS.md` are respected; I am not claiming local execution of checks I did not run.
- The intermediate superfix build's `075`–`088` SQL is unverifiable from this repo state (those files never existed on `0.1.6`); I simulated their column additions from `consolidation.rs`'s field list. If any of those migrations did something other than add columns (e.g. a data backfill), that behavior is **not** reproduced by `069` and needs a follow-up trace.
- Whether an intermediate build recorded version 69 with a different checksum — which would trip `Integrity` and quarantine on upgrade — cannot be determined here. The code comment in `consolidation.rs` shows awareness; worth confirming against a real intermediate build before release.
- The committed throwaway updater private key still exists in `0.1.6`'s history. It is not the release key and no deployed client's updater is active against it (base `endpoints: []`), so the live risk is low — but **rotate `UPDATER_PRIVATE_KEY`/`UPDATER_PUBLIC_KEY` before the first stable 0.1.6 publication** and confirm the release keypair was never committed.
- macOS/Windows runtime behavior of the manual installer, pill dragging, and audio devices was not exercised.

---

## 6. Mediation plan / roadmap

Nothing here requires re-splitting a 1,039-file PR — that would cost more than it buys. The plan is to land **~5 small, independently verifiable commits** on the consolidation branch, in this order.

### Phase 0 — merge blockers (before any approval)
1. **F1** — switch `OpenAICompatibleBaseGenerateTextRepo` to `secureFetch`; add the "fetch used" unit test **and** widen the `csp-capability` host scan to every plugin-http call site, not just `https://api.*` literals. *This is the only blocker.*
2. Manual smoke: Ollama post-processing end-to-end + one `http://` OpenAI-compatible key, on the built desktop app.

### Phase 1 — land with the release, same branch
3. **F2** — bind endpoint and pubkey together; add the config invariant test (non-empty endpoints ⇒ non-empty pubkey).
4. **F3** — retire 71–88 by ledger **description** instead of by range; test that a future `(71, "…")` row is preserved.
5. **F4** — `wait()` on `open`, delete `dest` on non-zero status.
6. **F5** — confirm intent for `.microreview.yml`; if unintended, restore it.
7. **Rotate** the updater keypair and re-verify `Gitleaks updater-key scan` covers history, not just the diff.

### Phase 2 — follow-ups (separate PRs, low urgency)
8. **F8** — split `apps/preview` out (it is additive and independent), or add it to the lint path filter.
9. **F6 / F7** — reconcile the stated exclusions with the diff; move the ~2.5 MB evidence bundle and root agent scratch out of the release branch (external artifact + a short in-repo summary).
10. **Unknown #2** — trace the intermediate builds' `075`–`088` SQL against `069` to confirm no non-additive work was folded in silently.

### Phase 3 — structural (what actually prevents the *next* one)
These are the protocol's own Part III backlog items, and #208 shows why each matters:
11. **Change-size guard.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for small PRs; 1,039 files / +210k lines cannot be line-reviewed by humans. Add a CI job that fails (or hard-requires a justification label) above a threshold, and route oversized diffs to a mandatory inventory report.
12. **Consolidation-integrity check.** Assert that a consolidation head contains every commit of its target branch (`git rev-list base..head` containment) and that every absorbed PR has a recorded disposition. This is the general form of F5/F6.
13. **Complete the capability/egress contract test.** Today it only mirrors `https://api.*` literals; F1 was invisible precisely there. Make it enumerate plugin-http call sites and assert each URL's origin is in the `http:default` scope — that single change makes F1 impossible to reintroduce.
14. **Readiness gates.** Adopt the protocol's completion rule: a green CI + bot `APPROVED` is not a verdict. Required-but-unrun gates should present as **Needs Verification**, and this PR's review trail (14 `codeant-ai` approvals with 0-byte bodies) should not count as human review for a release branch.
15. **PR-triggered CI.** Every desktop workflow is `push`-only, so the green checks here come from an in-repo branch push. External contributions would land with **zero** CI. Add `pull_request` triggers (keeping the existing fork-secret guards) so reviews are not blind.
16. **Ship the review-inventory script** from Part III (`§19`) — base/head SHAs, changed commands, migrations, capabilities, workflows, nearby tests — so the next consolidation review starts from data rather than from 200k lines of diff.

**Bottom line:** fix F1 and this is a strong release candidate. The consolidation engineering deserves credit — the migration replay and the installer verification chain are better than the protocol requires — but the PR's own thesis ("consolidate safely") is undercut by an incomplete egress migration and a decision-log that does not match the diff, and both are cheap to close.

Question: review

please run a fresh, deep review of the current pr head. prioritize unresolved high-impact correctness, security, migration, capability/ipc, async/error-handling, and test-coverage issues. re-check every finding against the current code and post inline comments only for actionable, reproducible findings. this is a new review request; please review the current head rather than relying on prior conclusions.

Answer:
### Findings

- **Medium — Audio import silently permits symlink selections inside an allowed directory**  
  In `transcription_import_audio`, the picker result is canonicalized before calling `open_audio_import_file`:

  ```rust
  let path = selection
      .path()
      .canonicalize()
      .map_err(...)?;
  let file = open_audio_import_file(&path, &allowed_roots)?;
  ```

  This defeats the helper’s `FollowSymlinks::No` policy for symlinks whose target is also inside an allowed root. For example, `Music/link.wav -> Music/real.wav` is canonicalized to `Music/real.wav`, then opened successfully as an ordinary file. The helper’s tests claim that even an in-root symlink must be rejected, but the production path never passes the symlink path to the helper.

  Please avoid canonicalizing the selected file itself. Canonicalize/validate only the allowed roots, then pass the picker path directly to `open_audio_import_file`; alternatively, explicitly inspect the selected directory entry with no-follow semantics before resolving the file. Add an end-to-end test through the same code path, covering both an in-root symlink and a symlink whose target is outside the root.

- **Medium — `open_audio_import_file` still uses an ambient root open, leaving a root replacement race**  
  The function checks the selected path against canonicalized roots, then separately opens `matching_root` with:

  ```rust
  Dir::open_ambient_dir(matching_root, cap_std::ambient_authority())
  ```

  If the root directory is replaced between canonicalization and `open_ambient_dir`, the capability can refer to a different directory than the one validated. The subsequent relative no-follow open is safe relative to that capability, but the capability itself was acquired from a mutable ambient path after the authorization check.

  Open the allowed root capability before validating/deriving the relative path, or retain a capability-based root object for the complete picker/import operation. The regression test should rename the root and replace it between validation and open, then verify that the replacement root cannot be read.

- **Medium — HTTP response buffering can exceed the advertised 32 MiB cap due to repeated reservations**  
  In `execute_http_request`, the response’s `Content-Length` is first reserved:

  ```rust
  reserve_private_http_response_body(&mut body, initial_capacity)?;
  ```

  Then every chunk reserves its full size again before appending:

  ```rust
  reserve_private_http_response_body(&mut body, chunk.len())?;
  body.extend_from_slice(&chunk);
  ```

  `Vec::try_reserve` reserves additional capacity, not merely the missing capacity. For a response with a 32 MiB `Content-Length`, this can repeatedly over-reserve and cause memory usage substantially above the stated 32 MiB response limit, especially with many chunks. It can also make valid responses fail on memory-constrained systems despite being under the protocol limit.

  Reserve only the missing amount (`body.capacity().saturating_sub(body.len())`), or rely on `try_reserve` only when `body.len() + chunk.len() > body.capacity()`. Add a chunked-response test that verifies the buffer remains bounded near the configured response limit.

## Verdict

Status: Not Ready

Confidence: Medium

Mergeable: No for acceptance. GitHub reports the head as mechanically mergeable, but this review requests changes.

CI verification: Failing at the quality-gate level. The hosted build, lint, unit, integration, and native jobs pass on the reviewed head. CodeAnt Quality Gates and SCR report a rating C with 80 findings.

Reviewed head: `51621823bb4ba29d0b23019b38845476c7cbf56f`

Base head: `3a37f922ee5c2cccaedc34e4feac7c86c78f23bd`

The range is one squashed commit with 1,039 changed files, 210,495 additions, and 19,219 deletions. Six independent review passes covered release and CI, persistence and recovery, native security, frontend and state, cross-platform runtime, and an adversarial cross-domain pass. I posted 19 new inline blockers. Existing bot threads were used as leads and were not accepted without a separate reachability and impact check.

## Change inventory

| Area | Changed contract | Risk | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Release and CI | Production updater signing, release dispatch, secret scanning, action pins, package and native builds | Critical | Untrusted branch can reach the production key. Scanner policy and artifact provenance also need work. |
| Database | Consolidated migration, legacy retirement, startup recovery, quarantine, privacy wipe | Critical | Checksum recovery hides readable data, legacy private tables can survive a wipe, and quarantine copies outlive Clear local data. |
| Native authority and network | Private HTTP, saved endpoints, audio import, updater signatures, capabilities | Critical | Encoded path traversal, root replacement, custom endpoint transport, and unbounded signature waits remain. |
| TypeScript state and providers | Repositories, generation, transcription streaming, review state, retry and redaction | High | Data-loss, provider contract, cancellation, and review-state defects remain. |
| Native pills and platform behavior | macOS, Windows, and GTK geometry, input, animation, and review rendering | High | Native platform findings need focused OS coverage. Several existing bot threads remain open. |
| Preview and repository evidence | Preview app, reports, prompts, session artifacts, i18n catalogs | Medium | Evidence points at another SHA and the committed transcript is not a product artifact. |

## Findings

### Release and supply chain

- **Critical.** ` .github/workflows/release.yml:335` exposes `UPDATER_PRIVATE_KEY` to a build that can run from any `workflow_dispatch` branch. A write-capable collaborator can change a package or Tauri build script and export the key. The repository has no protected release environment and `main` is currently unprotected. Use a required-review release environment, allow only protected main, and check out the trusted commit before exposing key material. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088709865).

- **High.** `packages/rust_transcription/Cargo.toml:46` adds `sherpa-onnx-sys 1.13.5`. Its build script downloads and unpacks a native archive without a digest check, and no workflow supplies a verified library directory. A replaced upstream asset can enter a signed release. Pin a SHA-256 digest for every platform archive or vendor a verified build. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088710001).

- **High.** `.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml:55` checks out the pull request merge commit and then loads the Gitleaks policy and guard scripts from that same commit. A pull request can weaken the scanner and pass the trusted-looking job. Run the policy from the trusted base through `pull_request_target` or a trusted reusable workflow, and never execute pull request code as scanner policy. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088710065).

- **Medium.** `gitleaks.toml:15` excludes all test and spec directories, all reports, and the exact transcript from scanning. The current diff has 129 changed paths in those exclusions. Use exact synthetic-value annotations instead of path-wide exemptions. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088712718).

### Database and privacy

- **High.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/db/open.rs:214` maps a changed migration checksum to `Integrity`, moves the readable database to `mausvoice.broken-*`, and opens a fresh schema. The test codifies the unsafe result. A checksum mismatch must not silently remove access to transcriptions, settings, and keys. Preserve the database or require explicit user confirmation before quarantine. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088710382).

- **High.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/db/open.rs:188` retires every numeric version from 71 through 88 without validating checksums or schemas. Historical branch migrations add meetings, webhooks, snippets, and translations tables that the current consolidation and wipe do not cover. Validate a supported retirement manifest, migrate or reject unknown schemas, and test a real intermediate database through the wipe.

- **Medium.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/db/open.rs:73` preserves the full quarantined database, while `clear_local_data` removes only current rows and managed audio. Add a retention policy and delete quarantine copies on an explicit privacy wipe. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088713066).

### Native authority and transport

- **High.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs:918` compares raw saved endpoint pathnames. Encoded traversal such as `/proxy/openai/%2e%2e%2fadmin` passes the prefix check and can route outside the saved base after server decoding. Canonicalize decoded path segments and test request and redirect paths. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088710176).

- **High.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs:1457` canonicalizes the allowed roots, then reopens the matching root through ambient authority for the file open. A root replacement between those operations can redirect the relative open. Hold the authorized root capability through validation and opening. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088710275).

- **High.** The native model admission path verifies a digest during download, but `packages/rust_transcription/src/api.rs:649` accepts any existing non-empty model file during inference. Upgrades can reuse a stale or replaced model without the new integrity check. Enforce the pinned artifact policy at inference admission. The existing CodeAnt thread is on the same path.

- **High.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json` removes plaintext HTTP scope while `apps/desktop/src/repos/generate-text.repo.ts:202` still sends Ollama and custom generation through `tauriFetch`. The existing freebuff threads document the reachable Ollama and shared-base failure. Route generation through the private or saved-endpoint transport and test local and custom HTTPS streaming.

- **Medium.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs:2538` ignores audio cleanup failure and returns success. A linked, unreadable, or temporarily locked managed audio directory can leave recordings after the user is told local data was removed. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088712874).

- **Medium.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs:4347` has no request, read, or cancellation bound for the detached updater signature download. A stalled CDN leaves the fallback in downloading state. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088712977).

### State, provider, and review contracts

- **High.** `apps/desktop/src/sessions/transcription-stream.utils.ts:62` removes samples before `WebSocket.send` returns. A close or send failure loses the drained audio chunk. Make send success or failure explicit before removing the buffer, then add a close-race test.

- **High.** `apps/desktop/src/utils/chat-parts.utils.ts:182` can render a persisted pending tool call as queued when no permission record is linked. The approval control is then absent while the agent is waiting. Keep the linked permission or render a recoverable approval state. The existing CodeAnt thread has the same path.

- **High.** `packages/voice-ai/src/gemini.utils.ts:468` sends each function response as a separate user content. Gemini function calling requires all responses for parallel calls to be returned in one content block with multiple parts. Bundle the responses and test parallel tool calls. The existing CodeAnt thread has the same path.

- **Medium.** `packages/voice-ai/src/gemini.utils.ts:113` does not check the shared signal in its retry predicate. A generic error after cancellation can start another upload with an aborted signal. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088713344).

- **Medium.** `apps/desktop/src/actions/pill-review.actions.ts:36` parses native Open decisions through a type that omits `open`. The visible control does nothing and can leave review state pending. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088713161).

- **High.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/pill_process.rs:322-384` dispatches the new `review_decision` protocol only after raw substring checks. A valid review payload whose transcript contains `click` or `typed_message` matches an earlier branch and is misrouted before `parse_review_decision` runs. Parse the JSON once and dispatch on the exact top-level `type`.

- **Medium.** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/db/api_key_queries.rs:85` treats an explicit `NULL` transcription path as “leave unchanged”. The new settings form sends `null` when the user clears the field, so the old custom endpoint remains active. Use an explicit clear contract and add a save-clear-reload regression test.

- **Medium.** `packages/utilities/src/error.ts:7` misses common labels such as `client_secret`, `private_key`, `session_token`, and `password` at the tool and agent error boundary. Use one redaction policy and add table-driven tests. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088713234).

- **Medium.** The three native review renderers wrap and iterate the complete review text on every frame. Bound the rendered preview or virtualize visible lines, while preserving full text for insert and copy. The macOS anchor is covered by the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088713423).

### Repository and verification integrity

- **Medium.** `rust-toolchain.toml:1` changes the compiler for every Cargo invocation, but the Rust workflows do not list it as a path trigger. A toolchain-only change can start no build, lint, or test run. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088712789).

- **Medium.** `reports/pr207/evidence/current-gates.json:3` and related artifacts record other heads and PR 207. The evidence cannot verify this head. Regenerate it after fixes and reject evidence whose SHA differs from the submitted head. See the [inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088713498).

- **Medium.** `fully read this.txt.txt` is a 14,229-line captured session transcript. It is not source or reproducible evidence, contains email-like values, and is excluded by the scanner. Remove it and add a hygiene check. See the [file-level inline blocker](https://github.com/maus-inc/mausVoice/pull/208#discussion_r4088714311).

## Missing test coverage

- Release dispatch from an unreviewed branch, protected environment refusal, and trusted-ref checkout.
- Two-device audio sequence handling, reconnect replay, and cross-device session ownership.
- Migration checksum mismatch, supported legacy schemas, privacy wipe, and quarantine retention.
- Encoded endpoint traversal, root replacement, unreadable audio roots, and updater stalls.
- Custom and Ollama generation through the actual private transport.
- Gemini parallel function responses and aborted retries with generic errors.
- WebSocket close races, pending tool permissions, and review Open settlement.
- Long review text on each native platform and the platform geometry/input cases still open in existing bot threads.

## Verification
